boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Wilson's Wharf record (May 24, 1864) in Grant's Overland Campaign [May-June 1864]. The post belonged to Butler's Army of the James; the live NPS description is empty, so the frozen CWSAC description is the NPS/CWSAC narrative. Campaign-wide marches, captures, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Brigades; the frozen description gives Fitzhugh Lee's division about 3,000 men and Wild's two regiments about 1,800. The live force field is blank. Butler says the post was garrisoned by two regiments of Black troops and that Wild commanded 1,800 men. Wild says he had no accurate count of the attackers; his estimate is garbled in OCR ('and probably triple'); prisoners spoke of detachments from three cavalry brigades, with three guns.
claims.rationale: The frozen figures and Butler's 1,800 agree on the garrison; Wild's estimate is unreadable. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 165 total; the live field reads 166 (US 26; CS 140). Butler gives Union losses of 1 killed, 20 wounded and 2 missing, and says the enemy left about 20 dead and 19 prisoners. Wild's loss line is garbled but begins '2 killed'; he found about two dozen dead and brought in 6 wounded.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Butler's 1 killed and Wild's 2 killed differ; the Confederate total is not established by these reports.

open_questions: Hinks's and Swain's reports (read, not selected; Swain's garbled line appears to give the enemy's strength), any Confederate report and the returns remain deferred. Humphreys mentions Wilson's Wharf only as a May 5 landing place.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the Army of the Potomac's chief of staff, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan, and it shares headquarters papers with Meade's and Sheridan's reports. Meade's, Sheridan's, Hampton's, Butler's and Wild's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXXVI, Parts 1 and 2, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
